paragraphs.title: The Spirit Poured Out on All People

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh.”
easy.q: Upon whom will God pour out his spirit?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “your sons and your daughters shall prophesy.”
easy.q: What will the sons and daughters do?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “your old men shall dream dreams.”

medium.explanation: The passage says, “your young men shall see visions.”
The passage includes servants and handmaids, showing that God's gift reaches every level of society.
medium.q: What does the inclusion of servants and handmaids show?

medium.explanation: A vision is a revealed or supernatural sight.
medium.q: In this passage, what is a “vision”?

answers: Sons and daughters, old men, young men, servants and handmaids
Old men, servants, sons and daughters, young men
Young men, sons and daughters, handmaids, old men
challenge.explanation: The passage lists sons and daughters, old men, young men, and then servants and handmaids.
challenge.q: Which order of groups appears in the passage?

answers: The Spirit is given only for dreams
challenge.explanation: After the Spirit is poured out, the various groups prophesy, dream, and see visions.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the Spirit and prophecy, dreams, and visions?

answers: Old men see visions and young men dream
Sons dream and daughters see visions
Sons and daughters prophesy, old men dream, and young men see visions
challenge.explanation: The passage assigns prophecy to sons and daughters, dreams to old men, and visions to young men.
challenge.q: Which statement correctly matches the groups with their experiences?

paragraphs.title: Signs Preparing for the Day of the Lord

easy.explanation: The KJV says there will be “wonders in the heavens and in the earth.”

answers: Blood, fire, and pillars of smoke
easy.explanation: The passage names “blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke.”
easy.q: What will appear on the earth?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “The sun shall be turned into darkness.”
easy.q: What will happen to the sun?

medium.explanation: The passage says, “the moon into blood.”
medium.q: What will happen to the moon?

answers: After the day of the Lord
Before the great and terrible day of the Lord
medium.explanation: The signs occur “before the great and the terrible day of the LORD come.”
The phrase describes rising columns or large streams of smoke.

answers: Fire, blood, smoke, and a red moon
Blood, fire, pillars of smoke, a darkened sun, and a blood-colored moon
A red moon, fire, a bright sun, and smoke
challenge.explanation: This is the sequence given in the passage.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the signs?

answers: The signs precede and prepare for it
challenge.explanation: The signs are described as occurring before the great and terrible day of the Lord.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the signs and the day of the Lord?

answers: The sun becomes darkness and the moon becomes blood
challenge.explanation: The sun is turned into darkness, while the moon is turned into blood.
challenge.q: What change is described for both the sun and the moon?

answers: Whoever calls on the name of the LORD
Only the people of the land
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “whosoever shall call on the name of the LORD shall be delivered.”
The passage says, “in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance.”
easy.q: Which places will provide an escape?

answers: Those whom the LORD shall call
easy.explanation: The KJV refers to “the remnant whom the LORD shall call.”
easy.q: Who will remain among the remnant?

answers: Calling on the name of the LORD
medium.explanation: The passage directly connects calling on the LORD's name with deliverance.
medium.q: What is the stated condition for deliverance?

answers: As places where the sun becomes dark
medium.explanation: The passage says that deliverance will be found in Mount Zion and Jerusalem.
medium.q: How are Mount Zion and Jerusalem described?

medium.explanation: Deliverance means rescue or escape from danger.
medium.q: What does “deliverance” mean in this context?

answers: Calling on the LORD is presented as the way to be saved
Calling on the LORD prevents deliverance
challenge.explanation: The passage says that whoever calls on the name of the LORD shall be delivered.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between calling on the LORD and deliverance?

answers: The first are connected with deliverance, and the remnant are those whom the LORD calls
The first are the heavens, and the remnant is the earth
challenge.explanation: The passage first speaks of those who call on the LORD and then of the remnant whom the LORD calls.
challenge.q: What distinction is made between those who call and the remnant?

answers: The signs matter more than salvation
Those who call on the LORD will be delivered, and refuge will be found in Zion and Jerusalem
Only those who see visions will be saved
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes calling on the LORD, deliverance in Zion and Jerusalem, and the remnant whom he calls.
challenge.q: Which idea best summarizes the passage?
